title: US Affordability challenges cut across every state and local election
gist: Oxford Economics says cost of living is the primary midterm issue, driven mainly by higher oil prices from the US-Israel war with Iran, compounded by ACA subsidy cuts, data-center-driven electricity costs, tariffs and elevated rates. Required income to afford median housing hit $115,600 in Q3 2026.

insights.claim: Rising cost of living has become the primary issue in the upcoming US midterms, with higher oil prices as the central driver rippling into groceries, electricity and housing.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Affordability politics raise odds of policy shifts around the election; watch consumer-sensitive sectors.

insights.claim: The US-Israel war with Iran has pushed up gasoline, utilities and food, three non-discretionary categories that weigh most on low-income households.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Energy-war pass-through hits lower-income consumers hardest, a headwind for discretionary retail.

insights.claim: Southern states and metros are most exposed to cost pressures because they have the highest share of low-income households burdened by the cost of necessities.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Regional exposure map for consumer credit and retail risk.

insights.claim: The average US household needed $115,600 of income to afford median housing costs in Q3 2026, up from $111,500 in Q3 2025 and 75% above the $66,200 needed five years ago.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Affordability has deteriorated sharply; supports weak housing turnover and political pressure on housing policy.

insights.claim: Rising interest rates accompanying cost pressures have eroded housing affordability more than in prior years, and no metro has escaped, though coastal metros are most cost-burdened.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Rates, not just prices, are binding on housing demand across all metros.

insights.claim: Cuts to ACA insurance subsidies have forced many to drop health insurance, with Southern states seeing the steepest enrollment drops.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Healthcare coverage losses add to household stress and political risk in the South.

insights.claim: The surge in data centers has raised electricity prices, with Northeastern states bearing the brunt.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: AI buildout is creating a political backlash through power costs; a regulatory risk for data-center developers.

insights.claim: Tariffs have hurt Midwestern economies, with manufacturing-heavy Midwestern metros most exposed.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Tariff exposure concentrated in Midwest manufacturing metros.
